claims.claim: A method uses a trained neural network to create a soft decision tree that generalizes better than one learned directly from training data.
claims.quote: We describe a way of using a trained neural net to create a type of soft decision tree that generalizes better than one learned directly from the training data.

claims.claim: Rules extracted from neural networks preserve high predictive accuracy of the original networks and are comparable to decision trees in predictive accuracy.
claims.quote: Experiments demonstrate that rules extracted from neural networks are comparable with those of decision trees in terms of predictive accuracy

claims.claim: ARTMAP rule extraction produces compact comprehensible rules whose accuracy and complexity compare favorably to alternative rule extraction algorithms.
claims.quote: Simulation results consistently indicate that ARTMAP rule extraction produces compact sets of comprehensible rules for which accuracy and complexity compare favorably

claims.claim: Knowledge distillation of deep neural networks into decision trees achieves 1% to 5% better accuracy than vanilla decision trees at the same tree depth.
claims.quote: experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1% to 5%) than vanilla decision trees

claims.claim: Any neural network with any activation function can be represented as a decision tree with exact equivalence, keeping accuracy exactly as is.
claims.quote: The representation is equivalence and not an approximation, thus keeping the accuracy of the neural network exactly as is.

claims.claim: MIPS auto-distills RNNs into Python code via mechanistic interpretability, solving 32 of 62 algorithmic tasks including 13 unsolved by GPT-4.
claims.quote: We test MIPS on a benchmark of 62 algorithmic tasks that can be learned by an RNN and find it highly complementary to GPT-4: MIPS solves 32 of them

claims.claim: Decision trees trained on transformed CNN feature maps achieve performance as good as the CNN with minimum complexity.
claims.quote: We observed that performance of the decision tree is as good as a CNN with minimum complexity.

open_questions: How much accuracy is retained when distilling large-scale networks (e.g., transformers, LLMs) into readable programs or decision trees?
What are the computational costs and scalability limits of exact equivalence methods (S7) versus approximation methods?
How do distillation methods compare on fidelity metrics beyond accuracy (e.g., calibration, robustness, out-of-distribution behavior)?
What methods exist for distilling networks into human-readable code (beyond decision trees) and what are their accuracy trade-offs?
